targets.speaker: ALEX
targets.target: When does helpful medical AI become something doctors and hospitals are accountable for?

targets.speaker: JAMIE
targets.target: The simple version is this: the moment AI moves from advice into care workflow and responsibility spreads across doctors, hospitals, vendors, and patients.

targets.speaker: JAMIE
targets.target: The scary part is not the average result. It is the person, patient, team, or company living inside the exception.

targets.speaker: RUFUS
targets.target: Lovely. We have automated the decision and preserved the blame. Very efficient, in the bleakest possible sense.

targets.speaker: JAMIE
targets.target: Think of it like moving from a helpful second opinion to a silent co-pilot in the exam room.

targets.speaker: ALEX
targets.target: Do not ask only what launched. Ask what new permission, risk, cost, or accountability chain just appeared.

targets.speaker: RUFUS
targets.target: The question for tomorrow is not whether clinical risk transfer sounds clever. It is who gets caught when it becomes real.
